```{=html}
<div class="note-box">
Each article is the unit of analysis. Its thematic profile is stored with the article itself, and the overall radar is calculated from those article-level profiles. Scores do not represent article quality, journal rank, or scientific impact; they describe the relative thematic emphasis of each study on a 0–10 scale.
</div>
```

## Research profile

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6.2
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "90%"
#| fig-alt: "Radar chart summarizing the average thematic profile of the research portfolio across eight hydrology and water-resources domains."

library(fmsb)

mean_scores <- colMeans(scores)

mean_radar_df <- as.data.frame(
  rbind(
    rep(10, ncol(scores)),
    rep(0, ncol(scores)),
    mean_scores
  )
)

colnames(mean_radar_df) <- colnames(scores)
rownames(mean_radar_df) <- c("Maximum", "Minimum", "Average")

mean_color <- "#173F73"
mean_fill <- adjustcolor(mean_color, alpha.f = 0.18)

op <- par(
  bg = "#f7f6f2",
  mar = c(0.8, 0.8, 2.0, 0.8),
  family = "sans"
)

invisible(
  radarchart(
    mean_radar_df,
    axistype = 1,
    pcol = mean_color,
    pfcol = mean_fill,
    plwd = 3,
    plty = 1,
    cglcol = "#d8d5cc",
    cglty = 1,
    cglwd = 0.8,
    axislabcol = "#77736b",
    caxislabels = c("", "2", "4", "6", "8", "10"),
    calcex = 0.72,
    vlcex = 0.82,
    vlabels = radar_labels,
    title = "Average Research Profile"
  )
)

par(op)
```

The aggregate profile is the arithmetic mean of the 13 article-level profiles. It summarizes the research portfolio without assigning a separate score to a thematic block.

## Articles and thematic profiles

```{r}
#| results: asis

escape_html <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("&", "&amp;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("<", "&lt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub(">", "&gt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x
}

cat('<div class="article-grid">')

for (i in seq_len(nrow(articles))) {
  doi_text <- if (articles$doi[i] == "") {
    "DOI: -"
  } else {
    paste0(
      'DOI: <a href="https://doi.org/',
      articles$doi[i],
      '" target="_blank">',
      articles$doi[i],
      "</a>"
    )
  }

  article_scores <- as.numeric(unlist(articles[i, score_cols], use.names = FALSE))
  top_idx <- order(article_scores, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(3, sum(article_scores > 0)))]
  top_topics <- paste0(
    '<span class="topic-chip">',
    pillar_names[top_idx],
    " · ",
    article_scores[top_idx],
    "/10</span>",
    collapse = ""
  )

  profile_rows <- paste0(
    '<div class="profile-row">',
    '<div class="profile-label">', pillar_names, '</div>',
    '<div class="profile-track"><div class="profile-fill" style="width:', article_scores * 10,
    '%; background:', colors[i], ';"></div></div>',
    '<div class="profile-score">', article_scores, '</div>',
    '</div>',
    collapse = ""
  )

  cat(
    paste0(
      '<div class="article-card" style="border-left-color:', colors[i], ';">',
      '<div class="article-title">',
      '<span class="article-code" style="background:', colors[i], ';">', articles$code[i], '</span>',
      escape_html(articles$title[i]),
      '</div>',
      '<div class="article-meta">',
      '<span class="badge">', articles$status[i], '</span>',
      escape_html(articles$venue[i]),
      ' · ',
      doi_text,
      '</div>',
      '<div class="topics">Primary emphases: ', top_topics, '</div>',
      '<div class="profile-grid">', profile_rows, '</div>',
      '</div>'
    )
  )
}

cat('</div>')
```

## Interpretation

The portfolio is concentrated in surface hydrology, hydrometeorology, statistical hydrology, uncertainty analysis, and hydroinformatics. Water-resources applications are present as a secondary dimension, while river hydraulics is peripheral in the current set of studies.

Hydrogeology and water quality are absent from the represented articles. The radar therefore describes the actual thematic coverage of the portfolio rather than an intended or normative disciplinary profile.

## How to read the scores

The 0–10 values are article-level descriptors. A value close to 10 indicates that a domain is central to the study; intermediate values indicate a substantive but secondary role; values close to 0 indicate that the domain is peripheral or absent. The aggregate radar is calculated directly from these article-level values.
